EXPERIMENT — behavioral conformance-oracle PROTOTYPE run (2026-08-18). Validated Pattern B empirically against a temp store; artifact: docs/experiments/write_parity_oracle_prototype.py. Reused the tests' _FakeMCP/_FakeCtx capture + the interfaces sandbox-repo bootstrap; ran identical behavioral cases through the lib adapter (rebar.transition) and the MCP adapter (captured transition_ticket callable), classifying each as ACCEPTED / REJECTED(runtime rule) / PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED(surface can't express the input).

RESULTS (case -> lib | mcp):
A bug-close MISSING close_class        -> REJECTED | REJECTED   [PARITY — runtime "required iff bug-close" rule enforced on both]
B reason-required class, no reason     -> REJECTED | REJECTED   [PARITY]
C COMPLIANT not_a_bug close (w/ reason)-> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]
D caused_by culprit attribution        -> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]
E force start-work bypass (open->in_progress) -> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]

KEY FINDINGS:
1. The oracle flagged EXACTLY the three real gaps (MCP transition_ticket lacks reason, caused_by, force) and NOTHING spurious. Contrast the earlier naive signature-parity experiment, which fired on 4/5 ops with FALSE-POSITIVES (force_close/source/return_alias/_creation_channel) and was BLIND to the runtime close_class rule. The behavioral oracle inverts both failure modes: no false-positives, and it directly exercises the runtime rule.
2. The A->C trap is the concrete bug: MCP REJECTS a bug-close demanding --reason (B) yet cannot SUPPLY it (C). An agent on MCP is told to provide something the surface can't express -> a compliant reason-required bug close is UNREACHABLE over MCP today. Same shape for caused_by (D) and force (E).
3. Cases A/B prove the oracle verifies BEHAVIOR a shape/signature gate cannot: close_class is default '' on BOTH surfaces, yet the required-iff-bug-close rule is checked at runtime and both surfaces are confirmed to honor it.
4. force_close was deliberately NOT tested (deprecated, being removed per Ruling 2) — so the oracle carries zero exceptions and still catches everything real.

CONCLUSION: Pattern B (behavioral conformance oracle) is validated. It is the correct single mechanism: exception-free, false-positive-free, and it catches the runtime conditional-required rules generation cannot. The prototype IS the seed of the durable oracle (remediation ticket 2). The three gaps it cataloged ARE the MCP-parity bug (remediation ticket 1): add reason + caused_by + force to transition_ticket (claim_ticket gets force too).
